_comment: MODEL store (PLAN 2y). A model = a point in parameter space, plus the directions worth travelling from it and how far. Seeded from bank/morph_recipes.json, which stays FROZEN as the day-10 audit record and is never regenerated over. The AI edits this file in conversation (recipes, verdicts, tags) and bumps `rev`; the panel polls it the same way it polls morph_params.json. Validate with: node tools/model_bank.js --validate

BALANCE.name: balance only, 30 s (the keeper)
BALANCE.character: Held sonority, nothing moving but internal balance. The beating is between UPPER PARTIALS — the chord itself has no close intervals — so beating is available without writing unisons.
BALANCE.verdict: day-10 (keeper) — composer 2026-08-16: "Very nice. There were some very interesting parts that might have something to do with close intervals, like approaching unison. Lots of nice acoustic beating in there, and potentially at the same time volume changes. It did sound like acoustic beating and swelling, which is nice."
BALANCE.notes: Seeded from the day-10 audit record. NOTE: auditioned through two bugs later found in 2z G4 — morph pitch was out by up to 40.2 c on off-key onsets, and the panel carried the previous variant's dials across a switch. The material is good but any day-10 COMPARISON between models was of the wrong thing. Re-hear before blessing at MA4. See docs/SHAPE_LESSONS.md lesson 1. | 2026-08-17 (day 15), composer's ear: "the balance morph seems to end more abruptly than the others." MEASURED and true — it used to cut at 97% of its own peak (mean voice level 7.5/10, all 8 sounding) against 29-59% for the other five. Cause: this is the only model on dyn.shape `rotate`, and rotate at turns=1 returns to EXACTLY its starting level (p=0 and p=1 are identical), while `swell` is an arch whose ends are its trough. Not an M6 property — swapping the shape swaps the behaviour both ways. Fixed here in data, not in the engine: stock `carrier.release: 5` plus the `close it` recipe. See docs/MORPH_FINDINGS.md.

LGSPECTRAL.name: LGMF spectral — a set of partials through the reference to another
LGSPECTRAL.character: The chord begins on partials of the fundamental that are NOT the reference harmony, focuses onto the reference, rests there, and moves away to a different set. The vibraphone holds its bars throughout; the bass moves like everyone else (LG-30).
LGSPECTRAL.verdict: built 2026-09-19 by tools/build_transition_models.js (PLAN 1a.5) — NOT YET HEARD.
LGSPECTRAL.notes: One model per transition TYPE; the six chords are its six actuals (ACT-LGSPECTRAL-01…06). The pitch data is bank/reference_chords.json and nothing here is typed by hand — re-run the tool. The 30 · 30 · 30 profile is target.dwell = 1/3 against carrier.span 90; both are dials.

LGBLOOM.name: LGMF bloom — the deviations resolving onto clean partials and back
LGBLOOM.character: Every voice that sits on a deviant partial, or on no partial at all, glides to the nearest partial of the same fundamental with almost no deviation, rests there, and comes back. The vibraphone CANNOT follow — its doubling bar stays sounding 14–49¢ off the bloomed series, which the composer accepted as the fixed point (LG-30) — and the bass holds partial 1.

LGCONVERGE.name: LGMF converge — the beating pairs closing into unison and reopening
LGCONVERGE.character: His subject: "lots of friction and kinetic energy moving into something very clean and pure" (LG-31). The tempered double glides 14 / 31 / 49 cents onto the just partial; where the partner is a vibraphone bar the just voice goes to the bar instead and the unison lands off the series. The bass leaves the root altogether and mirrors the lowest voice above it.

TAKES.name: TAKE → TAKE
TAKES.character: His words (RUNNING_LOG §350): "I want to use the morph to transition between 2 takes." Take A → take B: each player slides from THEIR note in A to THEIR note in B, cents kept, the starts scattered so no two leave together; one typed duration is the whole transition. The vibraphones switch — a re-strike on the new bar, never a bend. Without two takes chosen it plays its own set as a plain two-station glide.
TAKES.verdict: built 2026-09-25 (PLAN 1t.1, Opus, session 15) — NOT YET HEARD.
TAKES.notes: `carrier.releaseHolds` (1t.4): the release fades ON take B — without it the engine's release runs every voice back to its start, a bloom closing as it fades. PLAN § 1t. Engine M3 with no `target.mid` and no `dwell` — the plain start → target interpolation (morph.js M3). The base names NO voices (`source.kind` is not `voices`), so `namesOwnVoices` is false and the panel reads the pulldown's takes: `from` into `source.voices`, `to` into `target.voices`, both by lane:seat (1t.2). `carrier.span` IS the transition under this model — the panel's one `duration` box writes it, and `carrier.duration` stays null (a body longer than the gliss folds everyone back toward A). The breath dials are PLAN 1j's defaults; `dyn` is PLAN 1s's standard, min pp · max ff (base = (pp + ff) / 2, amount = (ff − pp) / 2 on the table's level).
